name: Battle of Oriskany
note: The accounts put Fort Stanwix to the west of the ravine and the column's road running towards it, so the plan has the fort at the left. They say the Haudenosaunee lay on both sides of the ravine but not where along it, so one group is placed north of the road and one south. They do not say where the head of the column ended and its rear began, how the column was divided, or from which group the pursuing warriors came. The camps lay south of the fort; their exact place is not given.

phases.title: The column enters the ravine
phases.text: Herkimer's column marched towards Fort Stanwix and went down into the ravine and over the stream. The Haudenosaunee lay hidden on both sides of it, and the Royal Yorkers waited behind a nearby rise.
phases.quote: At about 10 am, Herkimer's column descended into the ravine, crossed the stream, and began ascending the other side

phases.title: The warriors open fire too early
phases.text: The Haudenosaunee fired before the plan called for it, and the Patriots were taken by surprise. Colonel Ebenezer Cox was shot from his horse in the first volley, and Herkimer's leg was shattered.
phases.quote: Contrary to the plan, the Indigenous warriors lying in wait opened fire prematurely

phases.title: The rear of the column flees
phases.text: The trap had been sprung too early and part of the column had not yet entered the ravine. Most of these men panicked and fled, and some of the warriors pursued them, leaving dead and wounded for several miles.
phases.quote: Most of these men panicked and fled; some of the attacking warriors pursued them

phases.title: The militia rally on the crest
phases.when: After about 30 minutes, with a break for a thunderstorm
phases.text: About half of Herkimer's men were still fighting 30 minutes in. They rallied and fought out of the ravine to the crest on its west side, and Herkimer regrouped them on higher ground during a one-hour thunderstorm.
phases.quote: Herkimer's men eventually rallied, fighting their way out of the ravine to the crest to its west.

phases.title: The Royal Yorkers advance in turned coats
phases.text: When the fighting resumed, the Royal Yorkers advanced with their coats turned inside out, to pass as a relief party from the fort. The ruse failed when a Patriot captain recognised a Loyalist neighbour, and close combat followed.
phases.quote: When the fighting resumed, the Royal Yorkers advanced, but the ruse failed when Patriot Captain Jacob Gardinier recognized the face of a Loyalist neighbor.

phases.title: Willett's sortie raids the camps
phases.text: Herkimer's messengers reached the fort at around 11 am. Lieutenant Colonel Marinus Willett led 250 men out to raid the nearly deserted camps to the south, driving off the few people left in them.
phases.quote: Lieutenant Colonel Marinus Willett led 250 men from the fort and raided the nearly deserted enemy camps to the south

phases.title: The warriors leave to protect their camps
phases.text: A guard ran to the field to warn the warriors that their camps were being raided. They broke off with the Seneca signal to retire and headed for the camps to protect their women and possessions.
phases.quote: They disengaged with cries of "Oonah, oonah!", the Seneca signal to retire, and headed for the camps to protect their women and possessions.

phases.title: The Germans and Loyalists withdraw
phases.text: With the warriors gone, the smaller number of German and Loyalist combatants was forced to withdraw as well, and the fighting at the ravine ended.
phases.quote: This forced the smaller number of German and Loyalist combatants to also withdraw.
